title: Smart Pointers: unique_ptr and shared_ptr
learningObjectives: Explain smart pointers: unique_ptr and shared_ptr.
Describe pointer/reference or lifetime rules involved.
Trace a simple memory access or ownership operation.
Recognize common undefined behavior and safety risks.
Choose a safer approach for a practical task.

understand.concept: unique_ptr represents exclusive ownership; shared_ptr represents shared ownership using a reference count. Use make_unique/make_shared and avoid shared ownership unless needed.
understand.whyItMatters: Smart pointers encode ownership and reduce manual cleanup mistakes.
understand.explain: Do not copy unique_ptr; avoid cycles with shared_ptr; use weak_ptr for non-owning links in cycles.

examples.title: Exclusive owner
examples.explanation: unique_ptr owns the object and cleans it up automatically.

examples.title: Observe without owning
examples.explanation: weak_ptr does not extend lifetime; it can check whether owner remains.

examples.title: Prefer ownership types
examples.explanation: Container holds unique owners; objects are automatically cleaned up.

practise.guidedTask: Trace the five Smart Pointers: unique_ptr and shared_ptr examples. Mark each pointer/reference's target, object lifetime, mutability and whether dereferencing is valid.
practise.independentTask: Build a small C++ exercise showing smart pointers: unique_ptr and shared_ptr. Include safe cases and deliberately describe (but do not execute) one invalid case. Demonstrate how ownership or lifetime is managed.
hints: Draw pointer arrows to live objects.
Use nullptr for empty pointers and check before dereferencing.
Keep pointer arithmetic within one array.
Distinguish pointer constness from pointee constness.
Prefer value returns, containers and smart pointers to manual ownership.

questions.explanation: weak_ptr does not keep object alive.
